A graph is now a reporting group, not one company: a parent and its subsidiaries keep their books in one graph, each closes on its own calendar, and the parent's statements combine them.

1.2.0 gathers everything shipped since 1.1.0 (September 19, 2026) — twenty-four patch releases, each with its own changelog. The through-line: the Closing Book finished its worklists (reconciliations, changed transactions), the journal and reports gained the verbs that were missing (edit, reverse, regenerate, file, archive), the console became a drawer on every page, and multi-entity turned the graph from one company into a group.

## Key features

**A graph is a reporting group**

- **Entities** — a holding company and its subsidiaries share one graph. The menu at the top right lists every entity of every ledger graph, grouped by graph in hierarchy order with its ticker, and it is searchable: a fund administrator's dozens of entities fit where a dropdown could not. Picking an entity in another graph switches the graph first, as before.
- **Entity → All Entities** became the selected graph's group: legal form, ownership, status, the month each entity is closed through, a Select action, and **New Entity** — name, legal name, legal form, ticker, held under, the parent's share. A graph's first entity becomes the group parent.
- **Every ledger page reads the entity in scope** — the Closing Book and all its panels, Live Statements, Home, Journal, Trial Balance, Inbox and Chart of Accounts. A single-entity graph behaves exactly as before: the group parent is the server's default and nothing new is sent. A page waits until the group's entity list has been read rather than defaulting to the parent's books, and says so if the list could not be read.
- **Combined statements** — on the group parent of a graph with more than one entity, Live Statements gains a Scope control: _This entity_ or _Combined_. Combined is the parent's Reporting Style over every entity's books, summed per concept, and the footer says how many entities it combined. It is combined, not consolidated: nothing is eliminated between them, so the parent's investment in a subsidiary and that subsidiary's equity both appear. Eliminations come with consolidation.
- **Entity Details** reads and edits the entity in scope and names its parent and the share held.

**The Closing Book, finished**

- **Reconciliations** — a worklist of each check that ties the ledger to something outside it for a period: status, both balances, the difference, whether it holds the close, and its review. Run them, sign off, release one from the close, and record a statement's ending balance for an account. The `unreconciled_accounts` blocker explains itself and offers _Close without reconciling_ only when it is the sole blocker. A comparison the books have moved past shows _Out of date_ until it is run again.
- **Changed transactions** — a transaction edited at the source after it was posted holds the close; now it is reviewed and settled in the app: what RoboLedger posted against what the source says now, by account, with the three treatments in the docs' words (restate, catch up, mark as handled), the recommended one selected and a refused one disabled with the reason. A change flagged again between Review and Settle is previewed again rather than settled at figures nobody saw. The close blocker says how many changes hold it and links to the panel.
- **Reopen** is offered only on the latest closed period, which is the only one the server reopens; the `unposted_source_events` blocker says what it means and where to clear it.
- **New schedule** takes an optional _Cost booked on_ date for a cost that went on the books before the schedule's first period.

**Journal verbs**

- **Edit a manual draft**, **delete** one behind a confirm, and **reverse a posted entry** with a date, memo and reason — every line shown with its sides swapped, and the API's preview checked before _Post Reversal_ is enabled. A closed month is refused in the dialog's own words. A draft's event is voided only when the API says it is the draft's only one, so a failed delete cannot leave the event half-removed.
- **When a row offers nothing, it says why**: a draft rebuilt from its source (change it there), an entry in a closed month (reopen the period), one synced from QuickBooks while it is connected (correct it in QuickBooks), or any entry while the close publishes to QuickBooks — a reversal posts in RoboLedger only.

**Reports, through their lifecycle**

- **Regenerate, review and file** from the report page. Regenerate rebuilds in place from the ledger as it stands; Mark under review and Return to draft; File report behind a confirm that says filing cannot be undone. The share dialog warns when a report is still Draft or Under Review.
- **Archive, unarchive, delete**, with a Current / Archived toggle on the list and a Filing column beside Generation. A filed report is a record: it archives, never deletes.
- **Rendered from the holon first**, the Tavi as fallback, since a report is now published as a holon. The downloads are Tavi (JSON), Holon (JSON-LD) and XBRL 2.1.
- A preset names its cadence (monthly, quarterly, annual), so a report is no longer labelled quarterly by default.

**The console, docked**

- The console is a **bottom drawer on every page** (Console · Ctrl+`), resizable and remembered per browser, and the only way in: `/console`redirects to Home with the drawer open. From the Explorer or Plan,`/do <change>` runs the author operator, shows a receipt of what changed, and the page reloads in place. Counterparties, the Inbox and the Reports list reload the same way.
- **Explorer and Plan refetch** when the tab regains focus, so a write made from an MCP chat client shows up without a manual refresh.
- **Plan rounds to a materiality scale** — thousands once the median monetary line reaches $10,000, with an _In thousands_ caption, `$` only on a section's first row and on subtotals, and a `$` / `$K` toggle. Exports keep full values.

**The public site**

- The landing page was rebuilt for the finance lead, with animated product demos in place of static previews and the close placed last: connect your books, ask and plan, approve the close. The demos are plain ES modules that the content machine renders frame by frame for the social cuts, so one source drives the page and the videos. Phone layouts for every demo.
- **Product pages**, starting with `/quickbooks-mcp`, built from one registry that derives the metadata, structured data, sitemap entry, `llms.txt` line and footer link, with a test against the SEO checklist. `/llms.txt` is served, new URLs are announced to IndexNow, and the site publishes as RoboSystems by `@id` with RoboLedger as the site name.
- On mobile the secondary sidebars collapse and dense rows give ground.

## Changed and removed

- **Entity → All Entities no longer lists one company per graph across all your graphs.** It lists the selected graph's reporting group, and it is gated like every other ledger page, so it needs a RoboLedger graph selected. Every graph's entities are reached from the menu at the top right.
- The **JSON-LD bundle** download is gone from the report page: the API retired it, the Tavi is the anchor and the holon the renderer.
- The **Console** sidebar item is gone; the drawer is the way in.
- The landing copy no longer says one connector per company: companies that report together share one graph, and the connector is per graph.
- Calendar-year presets are labelled "2026", not "FY 2026".

## Bug fixes

- Ledger pages act only on the selected graph, and only when it is a RoboLedger graph; otherwise they show a "select a RoboLedger graph" prompt instead of quietly using the first ledger graph.
- Connections: a refused action shows the server's reason instead of a success toast; a 409 row lock reads as retryable; a failed list clears stale cards; a failed poll no longer drops sync watches.
- Auto-Map waits for its job instead of guessing five seconds; a lock conflict in the Inbox offers _Try again_; deleting a publish list asks first.
- Schedules deduct salvage value the way the server does, and refuse an invalid one.
- The production CSP `connect-src` list is chosen by environment rather than request hostname, so deployed builds get the production list.
- A report's lifecycle confirm stays open while its request runs.
- Each signed-in section's own page is disallowed to crawlers.

## Platform and infrastructure

- **`@robosystems/client` 1.17.2 → 2.8.1** — 2.0.0 was the OpenAPI retag (SDK paths follow the API's tags), and the minors since carry the reconciliation, report lifecycle, changed-transaction, graph-selection and entity facades this release calls. **`@robosystems/core` 0.9.5 → 0.14.0** — the console drawer, `/do`, graph-write notifications, and the selected graph persisted across the apps. **`@robosystems/report-components` 0.7.0 → 0.8.1**. Next.js 16.3.8; Node 24.21 base image, now visible to Dependabot.
- **Deploying 1.2.0** — requires RoboSystems API **v1.16.4 or later** (`create-entity`, the entity arguments on the ledger reads, `consolidated` on live statements); it is deployed. Nothing to set before the deploy: from 1.1.24 this release carries no CloudFormation or variable changes. Across the 1.1.x line the one setup item was the `ORIGIN_VERIFY_SECRET` repository secret for the report artifact proxy, in place since September 25.
- **A second compute route** — `template-ecs-express.yaml` deploys the app on ECS Express Mode for a fork in an AWS account where App Runner is closed to new customers. `APP_COMPUTE` picks it and is unset here, so our deploys are unchanged. Permissions boundaries sit on the app's IAM roles.
- **Edge** — the report artifact proxy validates its target, client IP attribution is hardened, the image optimizer is limited to known hosts, and social cards are cached at the edge.
- **CI** — Docker Hub publishing over OIDC; base-image pulls authenticated against ECR Public; CI credential scope narrowed in the image build; the hosted runner image pinned. The claude.ai/design sync tooling was removed. A NOTICE file carries trademark attribution.
